issues.legal_issue: A revisional court reviewing an eviction order made under a summary procedure may not act as an appellate court by reappreciating the evidence and substituting its own findings.
material_facts: A special statutory procedure placed the eviction application before a competent authority, with no appeal and only a revision to the High Court.
The High Court reconsidered the evidence and substituted its own findings for those of the competent authority.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its limited revisional jurisdiction, and its order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 31F of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 provides limited revision to satisfy the High Court that the competent authority's order is according to law. The introduction of Part IIA created a summary procedure and made the competent authority's order final subject to that revision; the revisional court is not to reappreciate evidence as an appellate court.

predicates.summary_eviction_revision: The proceeding was a revision challenging an eviction order made through a summary statutory procedure.
predicates.competent_authority_made_findings: The competent authority made findings on the application after considering the evidence.
predicates.revisional_court_reappreciated_evidence: The revisional court reconsidered the evidence and substituted its own findings for those of the competent authority.

issues.definition: When a revision challenges an eviction order made through a summary procedure and the revisional court reconsiders evidence underlying the competent authority's findings, the revisional court exceeds its jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A certificate required for a qualifying landlord's summary eviction application is conclusive evidence of the facts it states, and a revisional court may not disregard it by independently re-evaluating those facts.
material_facts: The landlady produced a certificate from an authorized officer stating that she held a scientific post and did not possess another suitable residence in the locality.

The High Court accepted that the certificate was conclusive as to its stated facts but went beyond it to assess the landlady's duties and to reject the certificate based on its own evaluation and minor errors.
The landlady's appointment as a scientific officer had also been notified by presidential order.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in going behind the certificate or rejecting it on the grounds it gave.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13A1(1)(A)(ii) and (b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 permits a qualifying scientific landlord to seek possession on bona fide requirement upon producing the prescribed certificate; Section 13A1(2) makes the certificate conclusive evidence of the facts stated in it. In Shivram Anand Shiroor v. Radhabai Shantram Kowshik, the Court explained the conclusive effect of a certificate under Section 13A1 and distinguished those certified facts from the separate requirement to establish bona fide need. Winifred Ross v. Ivy Fonseca was also noted in that discussion.

rule.if: summary_eviction_application and qualifying_landlord_certificate_produced and certificate_states_eligibility_facts and revisional_court_rejected_stated_facts_by_reassessment

predicates.summary_eviction_application: The proceeding was an application to recover possession through a special summary eviction procedure.
predicates.qualifying_landlord_certificate_produced: The landlord produced a certificate issued by an authorized officer for the purpose of the application.
predicates.certificate_states_eligibility_facts: The certificate stated facts about the landlord's qualifying status and lack of another suitable residence.
predicates.revisional_court_rejected_stated_facts_b: The revisional court independently reassessed the stated facts and rejected the certificate on that basis.

issues.definition: When a landlord uses a summary eviction procedure and produces an authorized certificate stating eligibility facts, those facts must be accepted if the revisional court rejects them by reassessing them.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional court may not disturb a competent authority's finding of bona fide requirement merely because another view of the evidence is possible; intervention requires a perverse or unreasonable finding.
material_facts: The competent authority found that the landlady bona fide required the premises after considering evidence that relations in the household were strained and that continued joint living was no longer possible.
The High Court reanalysed the evidence and concluded that the landlady could continue living in the portion she occupied.
The Supreme Court found that the competent authority's finding was not perverse or unreasonable.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in reversing the competent authority's finding of bona fide requirement.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13A1(1)(A)(ii) requires bona fide need for occupation, which is distinct from the facts conclusively established by the prescribed certificate. Shivram Anand Shiroor v. Radhabai Shantram Kowshik recognizes that the landlord must establish bona fide requirement even where the certificate conclusively establishes other specified facts. The Court applied the settled principle that a revisional court should not interfere with a finding merely because another view is possible on reappreciation of evidence; the finding must be perverse or unreasonable to warrant interference.

rule.if: summary_eviction_revision and competent_authority_found_bona_fide_need and finding_supported_by_evidence and not finding_perverse_or_unreasonable and revisional_court_reversed_finding_on_reappraisal

predicates.summary_eviction_revision: The proceeding was a revision challenging an eviction order made through a summary statutory procedure.
predicates.competent_authority_found_bona_fide_need: The competent authority found that the landlord genuinely required the premises for occupation.
predicates.finding_supported_by_evidence: The competent authority based its finding on evidence presented in the proceeding.
predicates.finding_perverse_or_unreasonable: The competent authority's finding was so unsupported or unreasonable that it could not properly stand.
predicates.revisional_court_reversed_finding_on_rea: The revisional court reversed the finding after independently reconsidering the evidence.

issues.definition: When a competent authority finds bona fide need on the evidence and its finding is not perverse or unreasonable, a revisional court cannot reverse it merely by reappraising the evidence.
